thread:
incident-bot: :alert: DETECTED: spike in tail latency in canary after rolling deploy airwave-v3 (region: us-west). Auto-page SEV2.

deploy-bot: deploy airwave-v3 initiated 1766667001, canary batch 1/8. CI green.

alex: p95 -> p99 divergence on canary hosts, kernel selector logs show fallback to scalar GEMM under load. Dumping snippets.

oliver: saw repeated 'kernel_select: selected=fallback_scalar' around 16:12:02, correlates with token latencies jumping.

alex: paste: ```
[16:12:00] kernel_select: model=airwave-v3, seq_len=1024, hw=rtx-a2, selected=fast_gemm
[16:12:02] kernel_select: model=airwave-v3, seq_len=1024, hw=rtx-a2, selected=fallback_scalar
[16:12:02] token_latency_ms: 0.14 -> 1.52
```

maya (oncall): Paging in. Is this prefetch/pacing related? Any QPS spike?

ryan (sre): Traffic to canary steady. Post-deploy telemetry shows microbatch alignment changed: batching window jittered upward, causing larger effective batch sizes. That plus kernel selector threshold==> fallback.

carla (release): We have a canary-only feature flag airwave_prefetch that enables aggressive prefetch/batching. Recommend kill-switch on canary to test.

alex: Agree. Flip the flag for canary; if tails fall, then either pause rollout or rollback.

leah (cs): Noting 3 enterprise canary customers reported timeouts in internal smoke tests. They flagged to CS. No major escalations yet.

deploy-bot: ffctl cmd available: ffctl set airwave_prefetch=false --env canary --by=release

maya (oncall): Flipping now and watching p99 for 10m.

maya (oncall): ffctl set airwave_prefetch=false --env canary -> OK (1766667120)

incident-bot: Action recorded: feature flag airwave_prefetch=false applied to canary by maya. Observe 10m correlation window.

oliver: Initial reaction: p95 down ~28%, p99 still high but dropping. Kernel fallback frequency decreasing.

ryan (sre): Some canary pods still hitting fallback because local KV cache warmed under the previous larger batch sizing. Suggest rolling restart to clear caches on subset.

alex: Propose rolling-restart 3/8 canary pods to rebalance KV/cache state and kernel path selection.

carla (release): Approve. Command: kubectl rollout restart deploy/airwave-canary -n inference --max-unavailable=1.

deploy-bot: Rollout restart queued and executed (1766667240).

leah (cs): Sending customer comms: heads-up to affected accounts, estimate mitigation in 20-30m.

ben (product): If canary stabilizes, hold automated rollout. Run extended perf smoke and add gating for kernel selector behavior.

maya (oncall): Handoff in 30m to oliver (@oliver takes lead if unresolved). Marking oncall-handoff.

oliver: Taking lead after restart. Tightening p99 alert: >800ms escalate to SEV1. I'll post updates every 15m.

deploy-bot: Rolling restart progressed: 3/8 pods restarted. Observability: p99 trending from ~1.2s -> ~420ms. (1766667360)

alex: Kernel logs show stable selection of optimized GEMM kernels after restarts. Good sign.

incident-bot: Interim customer impact: contained to canary cohort; ~3 customers saw degraded perf. Severity remains SEV2.

leah (cs): Customers acknowledged comms; one requested temporary routing to stable pool — offered and queued.

carla (release): Decision: pause automated rollout. Run 2h extended smoke on canary with prefetch off, then decide rollforward vs rollback. Vote?

ben (product): Vote to hold and run smoke. Also schedule infra work to add kernel-selection telemetry across batch distributions.

alex: I'll own postmortem action item: add gating test for kernel selector under new batch distributions and add canary-only perf probe.

maya (oncall): Handing off to oliver for monitoring. If oliver marks stable after 120m, close incident and block automated rollouts until fix.

oliver: 15m update: p95=92ms, p99=380ms, no new errors from customers. Continuing to monitor.

incident-bot: Escalation rule posted: if p99 > 800ms -> SEV1 and notify exec-oncall.

oliver: 120m update (1766667601): metrics stable, no new customer impact. Recommend close and keep rollout paused until follow-up changes land.

carla (release): Agreed. Closing incident. Postmortem items assigned.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (SEV2 -> resolved). Final mitigations: canary feature flag flip + partial rolling restart. Impact: canary cohort degraded only. Next steps: postmortem, add kernel telemetry, add gating tests, block automated rollout until fix.
